name: Eshban
overview: Eshban was a male Edomite, identified in Scripture as the son of Dishon. His mention is brief and specific, with no additional notes or expanded narrative provided in the biblical text. As an Edomite, he belonged to the lineage descending from Esau, reflecting the broader genealogical records of the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Eshban means 'man of understanding' in the original language, which may reflect a characteristic or hoped-for trait. This is the only recorded name for him, and it is not indicated that the name was given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eshban as the son of Dishon. Beyond this direct paternal relationship, no other family ties or relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning Eshban.
scriptureSignificance: Eshban's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of the Edomites, which helps trace the descendants of Esau and the broader narrative of God's dealings with the nations surrounding Israel. His mention contributes to the historical and tribal context important for understanding the lineage and heritage of the Edomite people.
